region.text: the Saadi legacy (Marrakesh and the south, the Middle Atlas edge, the Oriental) that the compile hands the Alawis in 1660, without the Tafilalt

events.note: 1660: the Saadi legacy is not the Alawis'; they hold the Tafilalt, take Fez in June 1666 and Marrakesh in July 1668. The Alawi page lists Mawlay Sharif as 'sultan of the Tafilalt in 1631', heads its list 'Sultans of the Tafilalt and early expansion', takes Fez only in June 1666 ('secured the surrender of Fez in June 1666') and Marrakesh only in July 1668 ('In July, he captured Marrakesh'); the page does not say who held Marrakesh meanwhile. The saadi-sultanate dossier carries the Saadi land as nobody's from 1659 to the Alawi capture of Marrakesh in July 1668, but the succession hands it to Morocco at 1660 and the morocco_1666 keyframe then strips it again (695 cells), to be regained in 1668. [Review p1660-p1669: first sentence corrected; the page also has al-Rashid recognised as sultan by the Banu Ma'qil and the Ait Yaznasin in 1664 and Sidi Mohammed's base 'as far west as Azrou' at the same time, with no extent, so nothing beyond the Tafilalt is drawn for 1664-1665.]

region.text: the whole island of Ireland, with the coastal cells (Galway, Dundalk, Clew Bay) that kingdom-of-england's own 1660-1707 corrections cut out of its shape, because 'the dependency dossiers draw' them: the kingdom-of-ireland_1660 keyframe, 'the whole island under the restored Crown'

events.note: May 1660: the Restoration returns the island to a Stuart king, who rules Ireland as a separate kingdom. Kingdom of Ireland page: 'The kingdom's order was restored 1660 with the restoration of Charles II of England'; infobox 'Dependency of England (1542-1707)'; 'From 1661, the administration controlled an Irish army.' Seam repair (sm-05): the draft holds 218 of the Republic's 284 cells and all 60 of Northern Ireland as nobody's land from 1662 to 1690 (sm-05 item from p1690-p1699). Cause, read from the compiler: kingdom-of-ireland ledger/14 (split from the Commonwealth, no month) gives the island's own 278 cells to the counterpart, the Commonwealth; the Commonwealth's dissolve at the end of 1660 (ledger/16) passes them to kingdom-of-england as direct land; England's 1662 keyframe, whose correction cuts the island out because the dependency dossier draws it, releases them to nobody until the p1690-p1699 gain of 1691. This loss gives the island back to the kingdom of Ireland in May 1660, before the Commonwealth's dissolve, so the dependency keeps its land (drawn as England's vassal by the colonies.csv row 1660-1706). The region is the set kingdom-of-england's 1660, 1662 and 1691 corrections subtract (the island, Galway, Dundalk 25 km, a 12 km disc at 53.96 N, 9.86 W), so no coastal cell is left to England.

region.text: the whole island of Ireland, with the coastal cells (Galway, Dundalk, Clew Bay) that kingdom-of-england's own 1660-1707 corrections cut out of its shape, because 'the dependency dossiers draw' them: the kingdom-of-ireland_1660 keyframe, 'the whole island under the restored Crown'

events.note: Companion of events/3: two coastal cells of the island (Dundalk and Wicklow) are nobody's at 1 January 1660 and kingdom-of-england's ledger/99 (vassal_start of kingdom-of-ireland, May 1660) draws them as England's own land, so the Commonwealth loss of events/3 does not reach them. Same page and reason: the whole island is the Crown's Kingdom of Ireland from the Restoration of 1660 ('Dependency of England (1542-1707)'). Dated June so that it follows England's May event.

region.text: present Sweden: a gain moves only the cells Denmark-Norway holds there, the Idre-Sarna border cell(s) ceded at Bromsebro (1645) and any other Danish-Norwegian speckle

events.note: 1660: Jamtland, Harjedalen and Idre-Sarna are Swedish. Treaty of Bromsebro page: 'Denmark-Norway ceded the Norwegian provinces of Jamtland and Harjedalen'; 'The Norwegian regions Idre & Sarna were conquered by Dalecarlian peasants at the suggestion of the Swedish government', and 'The concession of this region was not formally recognised until 1751'. Denmark-Norway page: the Treaty of Copenhagen (1660) 'gave Trondelag and Bornholm back to Denmark-Norway' and nothing else. Seam repair (sm-05): the anchor of 1 January 1660 still holds one Idre-Sarna cell (61.7 N, 12.2 E) as Denmark-Norway's, and it stays so to 1669; the p1670-p1679 patch (events/0) takes the same cells in January 1670 and its denmark-norway_1670 override stops the 1670 shape from drawing them.

region.text: New York state: the western and northern land of the Five Nations

rulings.why: The thirteen-colonies keyframe of 1664 draws the whole of present New York as the Duke of York's province, and rule R1 hands the colony the 300 cells the Haudenosaunee keyframe holds from Lake Erie to Lake Champlain. The Province of New York page says the province had 'no fixed western border', that the territory of western New York 'was disputed with the indigenous Iroquois Confederacy', that upstate New York was 'occupied by the Five Nations', and that the Duke 'exercised little direct control'; the English capture of 1664 is New Amsterdam (surrendered 27 August) and Fort Orange (24 September), neither of which lies in these cells (the nearest is about 56 km from Albany). [Review p1660-p1669: dates corrected from the page.]

region.text: Sweden inside its present border: the Jamtland and Harjedalen cells on the Norwegian frontier that the Danish-Norwegian shapes of 1660 and 1662 still draw

rulings.why: Extends p1650-p1659 rulings/0 (1653-1659) to the window: against the current dossiers the 1660 Danish-Norwegian and Swedish keyframes both claim 2 Jamtland cells (63.2 N, 12.2 E and 64.5 N, 13.8 E) and the size rule gave them to Denmark-Norway, which keeps them to 1669. Treaty of Bromsebro page: 'Denmark-Norway ceded the Norwegian provinces of Jamtland and Harjedalen' in 1645; Denmark-Norway page: the 1660 Treaty of Copenhagen 'gave Trondelag and Bornholm back' and returned no land in present Sweden. The ruling acts only inside Sweden: the Norwegian cells both shapes claim in 1660 (Trondelag and the border, which the Copenhagen treaty returned) stay Denmark-Norway's.

the three cells of present Sweden that Cliopatria's Denmark-Norway shape of 1662 draws: Jamtland and Harjedalen on the Norwegian frontier and Idre-Sarna, Swedish since 1645

correction.text: The 1662 shape without the Gold Coast forts, plus the Jamtland, Harjedalen and Idre-Sarna border cells that Cliopatria's Denmark-Norway shape of 1662 draws; holds 1662-1669

keyframe_overrides.why: Companion of rulings/1 and events/5. Against the current dossiers the Swedish 1662 snap (47 cells added) sets Sweden to Cliopatria's Swedish shape of 1662, which lacks the 3 border cells Cliopatria draws in its Denmark-Norway shape (63.2 N 12.2 E, 64.5 N 13.8 E and Idre at 61.7 N 12.2 E), so once they are Sweden's by the 1660 ruling and event the snap would release them to nobody in 1662 and the end anchor of 1670 would have them nobody's (the p1670-p1679 gain from denmark-norway then has nothing to take). Treaty of Bromsebro page: 'Denmark-Norway ceded the Norwegian provinces of Jamtland and Harjedalen'; Idre and Sarna were taken by Dalecarlian peasants, and 'The concession of this region was not formally recognised until 1751'. The Denmark-Norway page: the 1660 Treaty of Copenhagen 'gave Trondelag and Bornholm back' and nothing else.
